name: Oasis
notes: Date palms over a fringe of tamarisk, poplar and fig with reeds and sedges at the water's edge, surrounded by bare desert; Saharan, Arabian and Central Asian oases.

traits.native_range: Tamarix aphylla, N Africa to Iran, salt-tolerant evergreen tree 8-15 m — Kew POWO
traits.trunk: short twisted trunk, heavy low limbs, wind-shaped

canopy.silhouette: grey-green weeping-twigged tree with a spreading crown

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny hair-tufted seeds sprout within a day on wet silt; the seedling has two minute cotyledons and thread-thin, jointed grey-green shoots. It soon makes a single fast leader clothed in drooping, apparently leafless jointed twigs (leaves reduced to tiny sheaths), like a young she-oak, then a broad, dense evergreen tree; it also suckers from roots.
growth.source: Wikipedia Tamarix aphylla (tree to 18 m; spreads by seed, suckers and cuttings); ICRAF Agroforestree (to 18 m, 60-80 cm dbh, roots ~10 m deep; fuelwood cut from the 4th year after planting); USDA FEIS Tamarix spp. (germination <24 h, seed viable only weeks). Height-age curve, first flowering and lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: ICRAF Agroforestree (flowers May-Jul in racemes; capsule ~5 mm; seeds 0.5 mm with a 3 mm hair tuft, 100,000-286,000 seeds/kg); Wikipedia (blooms July-November); USDA FEIS Tamarix spp. (insect cross-pollination, many-seeded capsules). Flower life, fruit set, ripening and crop estimated.

canopy.name: Date palm
canopy.origin: North Africa and the Middle East

growth.juvenile_note: Remote germination: the cotyledon stalk pushes the growing point down into the soil, then grass-like, undivided strap leaves emerge. For several years it is a stemless, spiny fountain of increasingly pinnate, stiff, grey-green fronds, often with suckers (offshoots) at the base, before a rough trunk clad in old leaf bases rises.
growth.source: Wikipedia (to 30 m, slow-growing; fruits 4-8 years after planting, commercial yields at 7-10; offshoots fruit 2-3 years earlier than seedlings; lives 100+ years when maintained); FAO date palm manuals (remote germination, undivided first leaves); height-age estimated from trunk growth

canopy.source: Palm of Sahara, Arabia, Mesopotamia oases; height 15-25 m. Oasis palm; suckers from the base. Standard floras and Kew POWO for the name.

traits.leaf_shape: fan or feather fronds in a terminal crown
traits.trunk: single unbranched columnar trunk (doum forks; clumpers sucker)
traits.petiole: long fibrous petiole with a leaf sheath

bark.notes: trunk covered in persistent diamond-shaped leaf bases in a spiralling pattern, brown, fibrous between; base ringed with suckers

leaf.notes: stiff grey-green pinnate fronds with V-folded leaflets in several planes; lower leaflets become sharp spines

flower.form: cream-yellow branched spikes bursting from a spathe among the leaves

fruit.form: dates 3-7 cm, yellow to orange ripening amber-brown, in big hanging bunches on orange stalks

appearance.silhouette: a stout rough-scaled column with a full spherical crown of stiff grey-green fronds and hanging orange fruit bunches; suckers at the base; oasis groves
appearance.refs: Wikipedia Phoenix dactylifera; Kew POWO; Palmpedia

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (dioecious and wind-pollinated, today hand-pollinated; fruit 3-7 cm, bright red to yellow before browning; 70-140 kg per tree per season, several pickings); FAO (kimri-khalal-rutab-tamar stages over ~5-7 months); dates ~7-15 g each

canopy.name: Doum palm

growth.juvenile_note: Remote-tubular germination: the cotyledon stalk drives the growing point 60-80 cm down into the soil, so the first sign is a single strap-shaped, pleated leaf. Stiff grey-green fan leaves follow from year 2-3, forming a stemless tuft for well over a decade (it may start fruiting while still nearly stemless); the trunk then rises and later forks into two, four or more crowns.
growth.source: PROTA via Palmpedia and ICRAF Agroforestree (germination 1 month to 1 year, cotyledon stalk buries shoot to 60 cm, first leaf strap-shaped, fan leaves from yr 2-3, stem after 18-20 yr in the wild, first fruit after 6-8 yr, slow growth); hyphaene.org (to 80 cm deep, first fork 2.5-4 m). Lifespan estimated.

canopy.source: Palm of Sahel and Nile valley; height 8-15 m. The only branching palm; forked trunk. Standard floras and Kew POWO for the name.

bark.notes: grey-brown trunk marked with leaf-base ring scars, fibrous; trunk forks dichotomously

leaf.notes: stiff fan leaves grey-green, on long spiny petioles; crowns at each branch tip

fruit.form: shiny orange-brown oval fruits 6-8 cm in dense clusters; gingerbread smell

appearance.silhouette: the only branching palm: a trunk that forks in Ys two or three times, each fork tipped with a round tuft of fan leaves; candelabra of tufts
appearance.refs: Wikipedia Hyphaene thebaica; Kew POWO; Palmpedia

fruiting.source: ICRAF Agroforestree and Palmpedia/PROTA (dioecious, wind-pollinated, flowers Feb-Apr in Sudan, fruit 6-10 x 6-8 cm shiny brown, ~120 g, ripens in 6-12 months, ~50 kg per tree, fibrous gingerbread-flavoured pulp eaten raw); hyphaene.org (orange to dark-brown epicarp). Set and rot time estimated.

canopy.name: Saharan cypress

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are almost never seen in the wild now. In nurseries the seed sprouts with slender cotyledons and a few spreading needle-like juvenile leaves before the grey-green scale leaves take over; the young tree is a dense narrow cone, which the wild relicts lost long ago to drought, wind and age.
growth.source: Gymnosperm Database and conifers.org (Cupressus dupreziana: to 20 m, trunks to 3.5 m across, about 230 trees left in the Tassili n'Ajjer, oldest estimated well over 2000 years, virtually no natural regeneration); Pichot et al. 2001 Nature (paternal apomixis: many seeds carry only the pollen parent's genome); growth rates and first seed estimated

repro.note: much of the seed is empty or apomictic; seedlings survive only after rare wadi floods

canopy.source: Cupressus dupreziana, Saharan cypress (tarout), relict endemic of the dry wadis of the Tassili n'Ajjer in the central Sahara, 10-20 m, massive fluted trunks to 3.5 m across, about 230 ancient trees, Critically Endangered — Kew POWO / Gymnosperm Database / IUCN

bark.notes: reddish-brown, thick, in long fibrous vertical ridges, greying with age; old trunks massive, fluted and partly dead

leaf.notes: tiny glaucous grey-green scale leaves on flattened, two-ranked sprays

flower.form: small yellowish pollen cones at shoot tips

fruit.form: oblong woody cones 2-3.5 cm of 8-10 scales, brown when ripe

appearance.silhouette: broad ragged grey-green cone on a massive trunk in a dry wadi
appearance.refs: Gymnosperm Database Cupressus dupreziana; Kew POWO; Abdoun & Beddiaf 2002

fruiting.source: Gymnosperm Database (cones 2-3.5 cm, 8-10 scales, ripening in the second year as in other Cupressus); timing, set, crop and decay estimated from C. sempervirens

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: two oval cotyledons, then small simple oblong grey-green leaves on a thin green stem while the taproot plunges deep. Young shoots are soft and nearly spineless; from the second season it is a low, much-branched thicket of rigid green stems with long yellow-tipped spines, and new shoots pop up metres away from its spreading rhizomes.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Alhagi maurorum: heavily branched grey-green spiny thicket to 0.9 m; rhizomes over 1.8 m deep, new shoots over 6 m from the parent) and Cal-IPC (spreads ~10 m a year from creeping roots, resprouts after fire and cutting). Hard-seeded; germination, growth and ages estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (bright pink to maroon pea flowers up to 1 cm; brown or reddish pods up to 2.5 cm, constricted between the mottled brown seeds; sweet 'manna' exudate used as a sweetener). Flowering months, bee pollination, few-flowered spiny racemes, pod persistence and crop estimated from floras.

shrub.silhouette: vase of upright stems, dark narrow leaves, pink flowers

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with two oval cotyledons, then narrow, leathery, dark green lance-shaped leaves in pairs or whorls of three, like the adult's. It branches from the base early into a clump of upright grey-green stems that becomes a dense, rounded, evergreen bush; wild plants line the gravel beds of seasonal Mediterranean streams and resprout after floods.
growth.source: Wikipedia Nerium (2-6 m; flowers Apr-Oct, peak May-June; wild flowers pink, 2.5-3 cm, in terminal clusters; nectarless deceptive flowers; paired follicles 5-23 cm with downy seeds; cardiac glycosides; sunny sites near stream beds); growth and ages estimated

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (Apr-Oct, heaviest May-June; wild pink 2.5-3 cm funnel flowers with fringed lobes in clusters; nectarless, few visitors, so fruit set is very low, cf. Herrera 1991; paired follicles 5-23 cm split to release downy seeds); very toxic cardiac glycosides; ripening and crop estimated

shrub.name: Pomegranate
shrub.origin: Iran and Central Asia to Pakistan

growth.juvenile_note: Seed from fallen, split fruit sprouts in warm moist soil: two small round cotyledons, then narrow glossy opposite leaves, bronze-red when new. The seedling soon branches from the base into a twiggy, spiny little bush; suckers keep coming from the root crown all its life.
growth.source: Flora Iranica / Flora of Pakistan (Punica granatum: deciduous shrub or small tree, wild in ravines and riverbeds of Iran, Transcaucasia and Central Asia); extension growers' data (seed germinates in 30-40 days, fruits from about year 3, bushes productive for decades, old plants centuries); ages partly estimated

shrub.source: Punica granatum, pomegranate, wild in ravines and riverbeds from SE Turkey and Iran to Central Asia and Pakistan, grown in the middle storey of every oasis garden under the date palms; deciduous spiny shrub 2-6 m — Kew POWO / Flora Iranica

bark.notes: grey-brown, thin, twisted and fluted on old stems, flaking in small patches; side twigs end in spines

leaf.notes: narrow oblong glossy leaves, opposite or clustered, bronze-red when young, red midrib

flower.form: scarlet-orange flowers 3-5 cm, crumpled petals from a thick red tubular calyx

fruit.form: round leathery fruit 6-12 cm, red to yellow-red, crowned by the calyx, packed with juicy red seeds

appearance.silhouette: dense twiggy bush with scarlet flowers and red globes
appearance.refs: Kew POWO; Flora Iranica; Wikipedia Punica granatum

fruiting.source: Flora Iranica; extension growers' data: flowers May-July, fruit ripens Sep-Nov about 5-6 months after bloom and splits on the bush if left; bees and beetles pollinate. Crop and decay estimated.

shrub.name: Henna
shrub.origin: North Africa and Arabia to India

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny seeds sprout in warm wet soil after a soak; seedlings are slow at first, with pairs of small elliptic leaves, then branch from the base into a slender, twiggy, much-branched bush that can be cut back to the stump again and again.
growth.source: Flora of Tropical East Africa and Flora of Egypt (Lawsonia inermis: glabrous much-branched shrub or small tree 2-6 m, leaves opposite, fragrant panicles); growers' data (leaf harvests from year 2, bushes cut for 20-30 years); ages estimated

shrub.source: Lawsonia inermis, henna, much-branched shrub or small tree 2-6 m of seasonally wet ground, wadis and oasis gardens from North Africa and Arabia to India, grown for the red dye in its leaves; fragrant cream panicles — Kew POWO / Flora of Egypt

bark.notes: grey-brown, smooth on young stems, finely rough with age; old twigs sometimes end in a blunt spine

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a tiny tuft of short, flat, grey-green blades. Within weeks it throws out flattened stolons that creep over the ground and root at every node, plus scaly rhizomes below, knitting into a dense mat; short erect shoots carry 2-6 finger-like spikes. Individual shoots are short-lived but the stolon-rhizome network persists and browns off in winter or drought.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Cynodon dactylon (culms 0.1-0.4 m, stolons several feet long rooting at nodes; acid-scarified seed 68% germination in 4 d; emergence at 17 C soil; flowers July-Oct; shade reduces vigour and canopy closure eliminates it); Wikipedia (dense mat, 2-6 spikes 2-5 cm, dormant brown in winter or dry season)

ground.silhouette: tall even reed wall with feathery plumed tops

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are small, weak, grass-like tufts of soft green leaves on wet mud. After a season rhizomes and long surface runners spread out; every spring new culms shoot up like thin canes to full height in a few months, with long, broad, grey-green leaves all along the stem and a big, silky, purple-brown plume that fades to grey-buff.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Phragmites australis (germination needs light, moisture and warm alternating temperatures after cold stratification; seedling survival very low; 3-4 years to viable seed; maximum height at 5-8 years; no part of a clone lives more than 8 years though clones persist far longer; culms die back yearly)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a small tuft of narrow, stiff, rough leaves. It quickly builds a stout, scaly creeping rootstock and branches from the base into a tall, leafy, harsh tussock; spreading rhizomes raise new tufts, forming dense stands with long, narrow, spike-like plumes that bristle with small spikelets.
growth.source: Wikipedia Desmostachya bipinnata (tall, tufted, leafy perennial branching from the base, erect from a stout creeping rootstock; N Africa to India and SE Asia; sacred kusha grass; fodder and a weed of wheat). Germination, growth and lifespan estimated from arid rhizomatous grasses.

ground.name: Sharp rush

growth.juvenile_note: Germinates in light on wet, brackish sand after rain or flooding: a thread-fine shoot, then a small tuft of stiff, round, sharp-tipped green leaves. Short rhizomes add stems each year until it is a dense, spiny dome a metre or more across.
growth.source: Flora of Egypt (Boulos) and Flora of Turkey (Juncus acutus: densely tufted perennial 0.5-1.5 m, stems and leaves terete and pungent, capsules 4-6 mm, glossy brown); germination studies on saline wetlands; ages estimated

ground.source: Juncus acutus, sharp rush (spiny rush), Mediterranean, Macaronesia and SW Asia to the Saharan and Arabian oases, with a subspecies in S California and Baja; dense spiny domes on brackish wet sand at springs, salt-marsh edges and dune slacks, 0.5-1.5 m — Kew POWO / Flora of Egypt

ground.name: Maidenhair fern

growth.juvenile_note: Spores germinate in about 6 days; heart-shaped green prothalli a few mm across form in 1-2 months on wet rock or soil, then two-leaved fernlets appear: tiny single fan-shaped leaflets on hair-thin black stalks. Later fronds branch into many wedge-shaped, pale-green leaflets and the creeping rhizome spreads a lacy mat over seeps and damp walls.
growth.source: Spore culture study, Not Sci Biol 9(4) 2017 (germination from day 6, heart-shaped gametophytes at 27-60 d, then two-leaved fernlets); clump growth, spore age and rhizome life estimated from growers and genus habit

repro.note: spores by wind and water; no flowers; needs a wet film to reproduce, so spread reads moisture not pollinators

ground.name: Bonfire moss

growth.juvenile_note: Spores sprout within days on ash, burnt or freshly turned damp soil into a felt of green threads, which buds into tiny pale yellow-green leafy shoots under 1 cm. Within a few months the patch bristles with long stalks that are yellow then orange-red, each ending in a nodding, curved, pear-shaped capsule; the stalks twist as the air dries.
growth.source: BBS Field Guide (Funaria hygrometrica: shoots to about 1 cm, setae 2-5 cm, hygroscopic, capsule asymmetric pear-shaped and curved; a fast colonist of bonfire sites, burnt and disturbed ground, garden soil); Wikipedia

repro.note: a pioneer: abundant spores from many capsules; short-lived patches move with disturbance

ground.source: Funaria hygrometrica, bonfire moss (common cord-moss), cosmopolitan colonist of burnt and disturbed damp soil, garden beds and the banks of irrigation channels; pale shoots under 1 cm with crowds of curved pear-shaped capsules on 2-5 cm twisting stalks — BBS Field Guide / Wikipedia

leaf.notes: small bulb-like yellow-green rosettes of broad pointed leaves

fruit.form: a crowd of 2-5 cm stalks, yellow then orange-red, bearing nodding curved pear-shaped capsules

appearance.seasonal: capsules ripen in spring and early summer
appearance.silhouette: yellow-green fuzz bristling with orange swan-necked stalks
appearance.refs: BBS Field Guide; Wikipedia Funaria hygrometrica

ground.name: Bird's-claw beard-moss

growth.juvenile_note: Spores and tiny broken shoots start on bare, trodden or compacted soil as a green film that buds into short upright shoots. These crowd into low dull-green tufts 0.5-2 cm tall whose leaves twist and curl inward like claws when dry and spread again within seconds of wetting; slender red-stalked capsules follow.
growth.source: BBS Field Guide (Barbula unguiculata: tufts to about 2 cm on compacted soil, paths, walls and arable fields; leaves with a short point, incurved and twisted when dry; capsules cylindrical on red setae); ages estimated

repro.note: spores and shoot fragments; dries out and revives in a moment

ground.source: Barbula unguiculata, bird's-claw beard-moss, nearly cosmopolitan on compacted and disturbed soil, paths, walls and field margins; dull green tufts 0.5-2 cm, leaves curled when dry, cylindrical capsules on red stalks — BBS Field Guide

leaf.notes: dull olive-green tufts; tongue-shaped leaves with a short bristle tip, twisted and incurved like a claw when dry

fruit.form: slender upright cylindrical capsules on 1-2 cm red stalks

appearance.seasonal: dull brownish when dry, bright green wet
appearance.silhouette: dull green tufts on bare trodden ground

ground.name: Common orange lichen

growth.juvenile_note: Begins as a speck of orange granules where a spore met its green alga on nutrient-rich bark or stone. It spreads outward a few millimetres a year as a rosette of flat, crinkled, overlapping lobes 1-4 mm wide, bright orange-yellow in sun and greyish-green in shade, soon crowded in the middle with little orange cup-shaped fruit bodies.
growth.source: British Lichen Society and Wikipedia (Xanthoria parietina: foliose rosettes to about 10 cm, lobes 1-4 mm, orange apothecia, greener in shade; favours nitrogen-rich bark and stone); radial growth of a few mm a year from lichenometric studies; lifespan estimated

repro.note: spores from the orange cups must meet a free green alga; no flowers

ground.source: Xanthoria parietina, common orange lichen, nearly cosmopolitan, on nutrient-rich bark of palms, tamarisk and fig and on walls and stones, North Africa and Arabia included; foliose rosettes to 10 cm of flat orange-yellow lobes with orange cups, greener in shade — British Lichen Society / Wikipedia

leaf.notes: rosettes of flat crinkled lobes 1-4 mm wide, bright orange-yellow, pale beneath, crowded with orange cups in the middle

appearance.seasonal: brighter orange in full sun, grey-green in shade
appearance.silhouette: bright orange rosettes splashed on bark and stone
appearance.refs: British Lichen Society; Wikipedia Xanthoria parietina
